name: set afterends
desc: Make Ctrl+Right and Ctrl+Delete stop at word ends instead of beginnings.

name: set allow_insecure_backup
desc: When backing up files, allow the backup to succeed even if its permissions can't be (re)set due to special OS considerations. You should NOT enable this option unless you are sure you need it.

name: set atblanks
desc: When soft line wrapping is enabled, make it wrap lines at blank characters (tabs and spaces) instead of always at the edge of the screen.

name: set autoindent
desc: Automatically indent a newly created line to the same number of tabs and/or spaces as the previous line (or as the next line if the previous line is the beginning of a paragraph).

name: set backup
desc: When saving a file, create a backup file by adding a tilde (\[ti]) to the file's name.

name: set backupdir directory
desc: Make and keep not just one backup file, but make and keep a uniquely numbered one every time a file is saved \[em] when backups are enabled with set backup or --backup or -B. The uniquely numbered files are stored in the specified directory.

name: set boldtext
desc: Use bold instead of reverse video for the title bar, status bar, prompt bar, mini bar, key combos, line numbers, and selected text. This can be overridden by setting the options titlecolor, statuscolor, promptcolor, minicolor, keycolor, numbercolor, and/or selectedcolor.

name: set bookstyle
desc: When justifying, treat any line that starts with whitespace as the beginning of a paragraph (unless auto-indenting is on).

name: set breaklonglines
desc: Automatically hard-wrap the current line when it becomes overlong \[em] that is: when it becomes wider than the value given with set fill (which defaults to the width of the terminal minus eight).

name: set colonparsing
desc: When a filename given on the command line ends in a colon plus digits and this filename does not exist, then snip the colon plus digits and understand the digits as a line number. If the trimmed filename does not exist either, then repeat the process and understand the obtained two numbers as line and column number. But if the doubly trimmed

name: set constantshow
desc: Constantly report the cursor position on the status bar. This overrides the option quickblank.

name: set cutfromcursor
desc: Use cut-from-cursor-to-end-of-line by default, instead of cutting the whole line.

name: set emptyline
desc: Do not use the line below the title bar, leaving it entirely blank.

name: set errorcolor [bold,][italic,]fgcolor,bgcolor
desc: Use this color combination for the status bar when an error message is displayed. The default value is bold,white,red. See set titlecolor for valid color names.

name: set fill number
desc: Set the target width for justifying and automatic hard-wrapping at this number of columns. If the value is 0 or less, wrapping occurs at the width of the screen minus number columns, allowing the wrap point to vary along with the width of the screen if the screen is resized. The default value is -8.

name: set functioncolor [bold,][italic,]fgcolor,bgcolor
desc: Use this color combination for the concise function descriptions in the two help lines at the bottom of the screen. See set titlecolor for more details.

name: set guidestripe number
desc: Draw a vertical stripe at the given column, to help judge the width of the text. (The color of the stripe can be changed with set stripecolor.)

name: set historylog
desc: Save the last hundred search strings and replacement strings and executed commands, so they can be easily reused in later sessions.

name: set indicator
desc: Display a \[lq]scrollbar\[rq] on the righthand side of the edit window. It shows the position of the viewport in the buffer and how much of the buffer is covered by the viewport.

name: set jumpyscrolling
desc: Scroll the buffer contents per half-screen instead of per line.

name: set keycolor [bold,][italic,]fgcolor,bgcolor
desc: Use this color combination for the shortcut key combos in the two help lines at the bottom of the screen. See set titlecolor for more details.

name: set linenumbers
desc: Display line numbers to the left of the text area. (Any line with an anchor additionally gets a mark in the margin.)

name: set locking
desc: Use vim-style lock-files when editing files.

name: set magic
desc: When neither the file's name nor its first line give a clue, try using libmagic to determine the applicable syntax. (Calling libmagic can be relatively time consuming. It is therefore not done by default.)

name: set minibar
desc: Suppress the title bar and instead show information about the current buffer at the bottom of the screen, in the space for the status bar. In this \[lq]mini bar\[rq] the filename is shown on the left, followed by an asterisk if the buffer has been modified. On the right are displayed the current line and column number, the

name: set minicolor [bold,][italic,]fgcolor,bgcolor
desc: Use this color combination for the mini bar. (When this option is not specified, the colors of the title bar are used.) See set titlecolor for more details.

name: set mouse
desc: Enable mouse support, if available for your system. When enabled, mouse clicks can be used to place the cursor, set the mark (with two clicks), and execute shortcuts. The mouse works in the X Window System, and on the console when gpm is running. Text can still be selected through dragging by holding down the Shift key.

name: set newbuffer
desc: When reading in a file with ^R, insert it into a new buffer by default. (The old form of this option, set multibuffer, is deprecated.)

name: set noconvert
desc: Don't convert files from DOS format.

name: set nohelp
desc: Don't display the two help lines at the bottom of the screen.

name: set nonewlines
desc: Don't automatically add a newline when a text does not end with one. (This can cause you to save non-POSIX text files.)

name: set nowrap
desc: Deprecated option since it has become the default setting. When needed, use unset breaklonglines instead.

name: set numbercolor [bold,][italic,]fgcolor,bgcolor
desc: Use this color combination for line numbers. See set titlecolor for more details.

name: set operatingdir directory
desc: At startup, make nano change to the given directory, and allow reading and writing files only in this directory and its subdirectories.

name: set positionlog
desc: Save the positions of cursor and anchors between editing sessions. These positions are remembered for the 200 most-recently edited files.

name: set preserve
desc: Preserve the XOFF and XON sequences (^S and ^Q) so that they are caught by the terminal (stopping and resuming the output).

name: set promptcolor [bold,][italic,]fgcolor,bgcolor
desc: Use this color combination for the prompt bar. (When this option is not specified, the colors of the title bar are used.) See set titlecolor for more details.

name: set quickblank
desc: Make status-bar messages disappear after 1 keystroke instead of after 20. Note that option constantshow overrides this. When option minibar or zero is in effect, quickblank makes a message disappear after 0.8 seconds instead of after the default 1.5 seconds.

name: set rawsequences
desc: Interpret escape sequences directly, instead of asking ncurses to translate them. (If you need this option to get some keys to work properly, it means that the terminfo terminal description that is used does not fully match the actual behavior of your terminal. This can happen when you ssh into a BSD machine, for example.)

name: set rebinddelete
desc: Interpret the Delete and Backspace keys differently so that both Backspace and Delete work properly. You should only use this option when on your system either Backspace acts like Delete or Delete acts like Backspace.

name: set regexp
desc: Do regular-expression searches by default. Regular expressions in nano are of the extended type (ERE).

name: set saveonexit
desc: Save a changed buffer automatically on exit (^X); don't prompt.

name: set scrollercolor fgcolor,bgcolor
desc: Use this color combination for the indicator alias \[lq]scrollbar\[rq]. See set titlecolor for more details.

name: set selectedcolor [bold,][italic,]fgcolor,bgcolor
desc: Use this color combination for selected text. See set titlecolor for more details.

name: set showcursor
desc: Put the cursor on the highlighted item in the file browser, and show the cursor in the help viewer, to aid braille users and people with poor vision.

name: set smarthome
desc: Make the Home key smarter. When Home is pressed anywhere but at the very beginning of non-whitespace characters on a line, the cursor jumps to that beginning (either forwards or backwards). If the cursor is already at that position, it jumps to the true beginning of the line.

name: set softwrap
desc: Display lines that exceed the screen's width over multiple screen lines. (You can make this soft-wrapping occur at whitespace instead of rudely at the screen's edge, by using also set atblanks.)

name: set solosidescroll
desc: When the cursor approaches the right edge of the edit window, scroll only the current line sideways by a large amount, instead of scrolling all visible lines sideways by just the amount needed to keep the cursor in view. This latter whole-window smooth sideways scrolling is the new default behavior. The single-line jerky sideways scrolling enabled by this option was the old

name: set speller """program [argument ...]"""
desc: Use the given program to do spell checking and correcting, instead of using the built-in corrector that calls hunspell(1) or spell(1).

name: set spotlightcolor [bold,][italic,]fgcolor,bgcolor
desc: Use this color combination for highlighting a search match. The default value is black,lightyellow. See set titlecolor for valid color names.

name: set stateflags
desc: Use the top-right corner of the screen for showing some state flags: I when auto-indenting, M when the mark is on, L when hard-wrapping (breaking long lines), R when recording a macro, and S when soft-wrapping. When the buffer is modified, a star (*) is shown after the filename in the center of the title bar.

name: set statuscolor [bold,][italic,]fgcolor,bgcolor
desc: Use this color combination for the status bar. See set titlecolor for more details.

name: set stripecolor [bold,][italic,]fgcolor,bgcolor
desc: Use this color combination for the vertical guiding stripe. See set titlecolor for more details.

name: set tabsize number
desc: Use a tab size of number columns. The value of number must be greater than 0. The default value is 8.

name: set tabstospaces
desc: Convert each typed tab to spaces \[em] to the number of spaces that a tab at that position would take up. (Note: pasted tabs are not converted.)

name: set titlecolor [bold,][italic,]fgcolor,bgcolor
desc: Use this color combination for the title bar. Valid names for the foreground and background colors are: red ", " green ", " blue ", " magenta ", " yellow ", " cyan , white ", and " black . Each of these eight names may be prefixed with the word light to get a brighter version of that color. The word grey or gray may be used

name: set trimblanks
desc: Remove trailing whitespace from wrapped lines when automatic hard-wrapping occurs or when text is justified.

name: set unix
desc: Save a file by default in Unix format. This overrides nano's default behavior of saving a file in the format that it had. (This option has no effect when you also use set noconvert.)

name: set wordbounds
desc: Detect word boundaries differently by treating punctuation characters as parts of words.

name: set zap
desc: Let an unmodified Backspace or Delete erase the marked region (instead of a single character, and without affecting the cutbuffer).

name: set zero
desc: Hide all elements of the interface (title bar, status bar, and help lines) and use all rows of the terminal for showing the contents of the buffer. The status bar appears only when there is a significant message, and disappears after 1.5 seconds or upon the next keystroke. With M-Z the title bar plus status bar can be toggled.

name: exit
desc: Exits from the program (or from the help viewer or file browser).

name: writeout
desc: Writes the current buffer to disk, asking for a name.

name: savefile
desc: Writes the current file to disk without prompting.

name: insert
desc: Inserts a file into the current buffer (at the current cursor position), or into a new buffer when option newbuffer is set.

name: whereis
desc: Starts a forward search for text in the current buffer \[em] or for filenames matching a string in the current list in the file browser.

name: wherewas
desc: Starts a backward search for text in the current buffer \[em] or for filenames matching a string in the current list in the file browser.

name: findprevious
desc: Searches the next occurrence in the backward direction.

name: findnext
desc: Searches the next occurrence in the forward direction.

name: replace
desc: Interactively replaces text within the current buffer.

name: cut
desc: Cuts and stores the current line (or the marked region).

name: copy
desc: Copies the current line (or the marked region) without deleting it.

name: paste
desc: Pastes the currently stored text into the current buffer at the current cursor position.

name: zap
desc: Throws away the current line (or the marked region). (This function is bound by default to <Meta+Delete>.)

name: chopwordleft
desc: Deletes from the cursor position to the beginning of the preceding word. (This function is bound by default to <Shift+Ctrl+Delete>. If your terminal produces ^H for <Ctrl+Backspace>, you can make <Ctrl+Backspace> delete the word to the left of the cursor by rebinding ^H to this function.)

name: chopwordright
desc: Deletes from the cursor position to the beginning of the next word. (This function is bound by default to <Ctrl+Delete>.)

name: cutrestoffile
desc: Cuts all text from the cursor position till the end of the buffer.

name: mark
desc: Sets the mark at the current position, to start selecting text. Or, when it is set, unsets the mark.

name: location
desc: Reports the current position of the cursor in the buffer: the line, column, and character positions.

name: wordcount
desc: Counts and reports on the status bar the number of lines, words, and characters in the current buffer (or in the marked region).

name: execute
desc: Prompts for a program to execute. The program's output is inserted into the current buffer \[em] or into a new buffer when M-F is toggled. When the program's name is preceded by a pipe symbol (|), then the current buffer (or the marked region) is piped to the program, and the output of the program replaces the buffer (or the marked region).

name: speller
desc: Invokes a spell-checking program, either the default hunspell(1) or GNU spell(1), or the one defined by --speller or set speller.

name: formatter
desc: Invokes a full-buffer-processing program (if the active syntax defines one). (The current buffer is written out to a temporary file, the program is run on it, and then the temporary file is read back in, replacing the contents of the buffer.)

name: linter
desc: Invokes a syntax-checking program (if the active syntax defines one). If this program produces lines of the form "filename:linenum:charnum: some message", then the cursor is put at the indicated position in the mentioned file while showing "some message" on the status bar. You can move from message to message with <PgUp> and <PgDn>,

name: justify
desc: Justifies the current paragraph (or the marked region). A paragraph is a group of contiguous lines that, apart from possibly the first line, all have the same indentation. The beginning of a paragraph is detected by either this lone line with a differing indentation or by a preceding blank line.

name: fulljustify
desc: Justifies the entire current buffer (or the marked region).

name: indent
desc: Indents (shifts to the right) the current line or the marked lines.

name: unindent
desc: Unindents (shifts to the left) the current line or the marked lines.

name: comment
desc: Comments or uncomments the current line or the marked lines, using the comment style specified in the active syntax.

name: complete
desc: Completes (when possible) the fragment before the cursor to a full word found elsewhere in the current buffer.

name: left
desc: Goes left one position (in the editor or browser).

name: right
desc: Goes right one position (in the editor or browser).

name: up
desc: Goes one line up (in the editor or browser).

name: down
desc: Goes one line down (in the editor or browser).

name: scrollleft
desc: Scrolls the viewport a tabsize to the left, when possible. (This function is bound by default to M-<.)

name: scrollright
desc: Scrolls the viewport a tabsize to the right. When needed to keep the cursor visible, it is moved to a longer line in the viewport. If there is no sufficiently longer line, no scroll is made. (This function is bound by default to M->.)

name: scrollup
desc: Scrolls the viewport up one row (meaning that the text slides down) while keeping the cursor in the same text position, if possible. (This function is bound by default to M-Up. If M-Up does nothing on your Linux console, see the FAQ: https://nano-editor.org/dist/latest/faq.html#4.1 .)

name: scrolldown
desc: Scrolls the viewport down one row (meaning that the text slides up) while keeping the cursor in the same text position, if possible. (This function is bound by default to M-Down.)

name: center
desc: Scrolls the line with the cursor to the middle of the viewport.

name: cycle
desc: Scrolls the line with the cursor first to the middle of the viewport, then to the top, then to the bottom.

name: prevword
desc: Moves the cursor to the beginning of the previous word.

name: nextword
desc: Moves the cursor to the beginning of the next word.

name: home
desc: Moves the cursor to the beginning of the current line.

name: end
desc: Moves the cursor to the end of the current line.

name: beginpara
desc: Moves the cursor to the beginning of the current paragraph.

name: endpara
desc: Moves the cursor to the end of the current paragraph.

name: prevblock
desc: Moves the cursor to the beginning of the current or preceding block of text. (Blocks are separated by one or more blank lines.)

name: nextblock
desc: Moves the cursor to the beginning of the next block of text.

name: toprow
desc: Moves the cursor to the first row in the viewport.

name: bottomrow
desc: Moves the cursor to the last row in the viewport.

name: firstline
desc: Goes to the first line of the file.

name: lastline
desc: Goes to the last line of the file.

name: gotoline
desc: Goes to a specific line (and column if given). A negative number counts from the end of the buffer (and end of the line). Putting ++ or -- before the first number will jump the given number of lines forward or backward.

name: findbracket
desc: Moves the cursor to the bracket (or brace or parenthesis, etc.) that matches (pairs) with the one under the cursor. See set matchbrackets.

name: anchor
desc: Places an anchor at the current line, or removes it when already present. (An anchor is visible when line numbers are activated.)

name: prevanchor
desc: Goes to the first anchor before the current line.

name: nextanchor
desc: Goes to the first anchor after the current line.

name: prevbuf
desc: Switches to editing/viewing the previous buffer when multiple buffers are open.

name: nextbuf
desc: Switches to editing/viewing the next buffer when multiple buffers are open.

name: verbatim
desc: Inserts the next keystroke verbatim into the file, or begins Unicode input when a hexadecimal digit is typed.

name: tab
desc: Inserts a tab at the current cursor location.

name: enter
desc: Inserts a new line below the current one.

name: delete
desc: Deletes the character under the cursor.

name: backspace
desc: Deletes the character before the cursor.

name: recordmacro
desc: Starts the recording of keystrokes \[em] the keystrokes are stored as a macro. When already recording, the recording is stopped.

name: runmacro
desc: Replays the keystrokes of the last recorded macro.

name: undo
desc: Undoes the last performed text action (add text, delete text, etc).

name: redo
desc: Redoes the last undone action (that is: it undoes an undo).

name: suspend
desc: Suspends the editor and returns control to the shell (until you tell the process to resume execution with fg).

name: casesens
desc: Toggles whether searching/replacing ignores or respects the case of the given characters.

name: regexp
desc: Toggles whether searching/replacing uses literal strings or regular expressions.

name: backwards
desc: Toggles whether searching/replacing goes forward or backward.

name: older
desc: Retrieves the previous (earlier) entry at a prompt.

name: newer
desc: Retrieves the next (later) entry at a prompt.

name: flipreplace
desc: Toggles between searching for something and replacing something.

name: flipexecute
desc: Switches from inserting a file to executing a command.

name: flippipe
desc: When executing a command, toggles whether the current buffer (or marked region) is piped to the command.

name: flipnewbuffer
desc: When reading in a file or executing a command, toggles between inserting the result into the current buffer and into a new empty buffer.

name: flipconvert
desc: When reading in a file, toggles between converting and not converting it from DOS format. Converting is the default.

name: dosformat
desc: When writing a file, switches to writing DOS format (CR+LF line endings).

name: append
desc: When writing a file, appends to the end instead of overwriting.

name: prepend
desc: When writing a file, \[lq]prepends\[rq] (writes at the beginning) instead of overwriting.

name: backup
desc: When writing a file, creates a backup of the current file.

name: discardbuffer
desc: Discards the current buffer without saving (when in the Write Out menu). When it was the last buffer, then nano exits with error status 2.

name: browser
desc: Starts the file browser (in the Read File and Write Out menus), allowing to select a file from a list.

name: gotodir
desc: Goes to a directory to be specified, allowing to browse anywhere in the filesystem.

name: firstfile
desc: Goes to the first file in the list when using the file browser.

name: lastfile
desc: Goes to the last file in the list when using the file browser.

name: nohelp
desc: Toggles the presence of the two-line list of key bindings at the bottom of the screen. (This toggle is special: it is available in all menus except the help viewer and the linter. All further toggles are available in the main menu only.)

name: zero
desc: Toggles the presence of title bar and status bar.

name: constantshow
desc: Toggles the constant reporting (on the status bar) of the current line, column, and character positions.

name: softwrap
desc: Toggles the displaying of overlong lines on multiple screen lines.

name: linenumbers
desc: Toggles the display of line numbers in front of the text.

name: smarthome
desc: Toggles the smartness of the Home key.

name: autoindent
desc: Toggles whether a newly created line will contain the same amount of leading whitespace as the preceding line \[em] or as the next line if the preceding line is the beginning of a paragraph.

name: cutfromcursor
desc: Toggles whether cutting text cuts the whole line or just from the current cursor position to the end of the line.

name: breaklonglines
desc: Toggles whether the overlong part of a line is hard-wrapped to the next line.

name: tabstospaces
desc: Toggles whether typed tabs are converted to spaces.

name: main
desc: The main editor window where text is entered and edited.

name: replacewith
desc: The 'replace with' menu, which comes up after 'search to replace'.

name: yesno
desc: The 'yesno' menu, where the Yes/No/All/Cancel question is asked.

name: browser
desc: The 'file browser' menu, for selecting a file to be opened or inserted or written to.

name: whereisfile
desc: The 'search for a file' menu in the file browser.

name: gotodir
desc: The 'go to directory' menu in the file browser.

name: execute
desc: The menu for inserting the output from an external command, or for filtering the buffer (or the marked region) through an external command, or for executing one of several tools.

name: spell
desc: The menu of the integrated spell checker where the user can edit a misspelled word.

name: linter
desc: The linter menu, which allows jumping through the linting messages.

name: all
desc: A special name that encompasses all menus. For bind it means all menus where the specified function exists; for unbind it means all menus where the specified key exists.
